:::{#exm-real-power}
#### Real powers, and $e^x$

- $2^3 = \expf{3 \cd \logf{2}} \approx \expf{3 \cd 0.69315} \approx \expf{2.07944} \approx 8$,
  which agrees with $2^3 = 2 \cd 2 \cd 2 = 8$ from @def-power.
- $2^{1/2} = \expf{\frac{1}{2} \cd \logf{2}} \approx \expf{0.34657} \approx 1.41421$,
  which is $\sqrt{2}$ (@def-square-root).
- For every real $x$, with base $e$ (@def-euler-number):

  $$
  \ba
  e^x
  &= \expf{x \cd \logf{e}}
  && \text{(@def-real-power, with } a = e \text{ and } b = x \text{)}
  \\
  &= \expf{x \cd 1}
  && \text{(}\logf{e} = 1 \text{, by @exm-natural-log)}
  \\
  &= \expf{x}
  && \text{(@thm-mult-one)}
  \ea
  $$

  So $e^x$ and $\expf{x}$ are two names for the same number.

:::
